title: Distinguishing Quintessence from Modified Gravity
bottleneck: An evolving dark energy signal can be produced either by a new scalar field (quintessence) or by modifications of general relativity on cosmic scales, and background expansion history alone cannot tell them apart. Discriminating tests require precision growth-of-structure measurements, which are contaminated by baryonic physics and nonlinear modeling uncertainties. Gravitational slip — the ratio of the two metric potentials — is the key discriminant, but measuring it needs both lensing and redshift-space distortions at percent precision.
why_it_blocks: Misidentifying the cause would send fundamental physics down the wrong theoretical road for a generation.
current_state: DESI redshift-space distortions plus Euclid weak lensing aim to measure structure growth at the percent level; current data cannot break the degeneracy. Joint DESI-Euclid-Rubin analyses later this decade are designed to deliver exactly this combination.
